newsitem.title: UK: UK parliamentary by-election set for Feb 27-BBC.
newsitem.headline: UK parliamentary by-election set for Feb 27-BBC.

text.p: The Wirral South parliamentary by-election will take place on February 27, the BBC reported on Thursday.
The writ for the by-election, which allows it to take place, will be moved in parliament on Monday, the BBC quoted ruling Conservative party sources as saying.
The by-election will be a key barometer of public opinion in the run-up to a general election which is expected to be held on or before May 1.
If the Conservatives lose the seat, which their candidate Barry Porter won at the 1992 general election with a majority of 8,183 votes, they will return to a minority position in parliament.
A recent opinion poll in the constituency made the opposition Labour Party odds-on to gain the seat, putting it 16 percentage points ahead of the Conservatives.
Porter died on November 3. By convention, the party holding the seat of a member who dies or resigns must move the writ for a new poll within three months.
